index_record.dataset_generation_caption:
The figure presents a simplified architectural model of a memory system and its interaction with cognitive processing components. The overall layout is divided into two main regions: the left side, enclosed by a brown dashed border, represents the 'Memory system', while the right side contains two vertically stacked boxes representing 'Cognitive information processing' and 'Cognitive functions'. At the top, 'External sensor signals' enter the system via multiple downward arrows pointing to the 'Sensory memory' module.

Within the Memory system, there are three primary modules arranged vertically. The top module is 'Sensory memory', depicted as a rounded rectangle with a light purple fill and dark purple border. It contains text describing sensory information, including environment data, information about other agents, internal sensory signals, and agent state information. Below it is 'Working memory', shown as a rounded rectangle with a light blue fill and green border, containing active information such as sentence fragments (tokens), flashes of images and video, etc. The bottom module is 'Long-term memory', a larger rounded rectangle with a pale yellow-green fill and brown border. This module is subdivided into two parts: 'Declarative memory' on the left and 'Procedural' on the right. Declarative memory further splits into two magenta-colored rectangles: 'Semantic', listing facts about the world, knowledge about concepts, and principles; and 'Episodic', listing information about experiences with associated context (time, place, emotions). The Procedural section lists task-specific skills, stepwise processes, and 'how to' task information.

On the right side, outside the Memory system boundary, 'Cognitive information processing' is represented as a light green rectangle with a dark green border. It lists functions such as information filtering, sensory signal conditioning, information fusion, symbol manipulation, self-introspection, memory reflection, and stored knowledge refinement. Below this is 'Cognitive functions', a light lavender rectangle with a dark blue border, which includes Perception (scene recognition, object tracking, speech understanding, pose estimation, etc.), Reasoning, Task planning, and Action execution.

Connections are indicated by arrows. External sensor signals feed directly into Sensory memory. Sensory memory sends information to both Working memory (via a brown arrow) and Cognitive information processing (via a blue arrow). Working memory also feeds into Cognitive information processing (blue arrow) and receives feedback from Long-term memory (black arrow). Long-term memory sends information to Working memory (brown arrow) and also connects to Cognitive information processing (black arrow). Cognitive information processing feeds into Cognitive functions via a black arrow. The entire Memory system is labeled at the bottom with a brown bar containing the text 'Memory system'.
